text:
Renee: Heads-up: onboarding streaming sample in staging started emitting duplicate side-effects after a transient 429. This one is interesting because it's a streaming client that retries the tail of a broken stream.
Kai: Streaming retries are messy. We have parity gaps: Node stream client resumes with a resume-token and avoids re-sending chunk 0, but Python currently restarts from beginning unless user supplies an application-level idempotency key.
Sumit: Oof. For streaming we can't just use Idempotency-Key on the entire payload. We need chunk-level safe replay markers and a short server-side window to dedupe.
infra-bot: [alert] 2026-05-02T12:03:02Z staging: streaming /v1/ingest 429 surge p95-retry=350ms
Renee: Proposed fix: 1) SDKs emit a `Client-Replay-Hash` header computed from the canonical stream manifest (stream-id + sequence-start + metadata) for advisory dedupe. 2) Server keeps a tiny sliding-window (4s) mapping of (stream-id, sequence-start, hash) -> last-accepted-seq and ignores reprocessed chunks below that.
Kai: That sounds doable. For non-streaming unary requests we keep behavior same (Idempotency-Key precedence). For streams we treat Client-Replay-Hash as best-effort dedupe only.
Sumit: Also parity: our jitter algorithms vary — Node uses full-jitter, Go uses simple exponential and Python uses fixed backoff. We should standardize to "truncated-decorrelated" jitter: sleep = min(max_backoff, random_between(base, prev_sleep * 3)) with base=150ms and cap=900ms. That avoids tight simultaneous retries and fits streaming semantics.
docs-bot: Note: recommend calling out exact formula and provide examples per SDK.
Renee: Small sample for canonicalizing stream manifest (pseudo JS) to include in docs:
```
// canonicalize then HMAC to produce Client-Replay-Hash
const manifest = JSON.stringify({stream_id, seq_start, metadata});
const hash = hmac_sha256(SECRET, manifest).slice(0, 18); // base64url
headers['Client-Replay-Hash'] = hash;
```
Kai: Make sure SDKs default to a short-lived client instance secret for HMAC so tokens change over time; servers only compare hash equality for short window and don't store raw manifests. Also avoid putting full payload into logs.
Sumit: Another edge: clock skew — if resume tokens contain timestamp, clients with skew may generate mismatched hashes. Keep the manifest strictly client-local fields (id, seq_start, metadata) and avoid epoch in hash. Server dedupe window should be based on arrival time, not token timestamp.
Renee: Telemetry: emit metric `stream.replay.advisory.hit`/`miss` and sample 0.5% of streaming replays with sanitized manifest for manual inspection in staging only.
Kai: UX: expose stream retry config in SDK constructors: `streamRetry: {enabled: true, strategy: 'truncated-decorrelated', base_ms:150, max_ms:900, advisory_hash: true}`. Default to enabled for onboarding sampleapp only.
Sumit: For immediate mitigation in staging: patch sampleapp to pause prewarm streaming and add `SAMPLEAPP_STREAM_ADVISORY=true`. Also add a CI test that tears down connection with a 429, resumes client with the same manifest+hash, and asserts sink has no duplicate chunk side-effects.
Renee: I'll open quick PRs: sampleapp patch PR 4732 (pause prewarm streams), server LRU-stream-dedupe PR 4738, Node SDK stream parity PR 4741, Python stream resume PR 4742.
infra-bot: [update] PR 4732 deployed to staging canary=8%. Monitoring 10m.
Kai: Follow-up: we should document when to use persistent application-level idempotency (payments) vs advisory replay-hash (short lived streaming resumes) so customers choose the right tool.
Sumit: Agree. Also add a short note on privacy: manifest hashing must be irreversible; HMAC is fine but avoid storing raw manifests server-side.
Renee: Action items recap:
- Renee: sampleapp pause prewarm streaming + env opt-in (PR 4732).
- Kai: SDK parity PRs for stream resume hashing + truncated-decorrelated defaults (PRs 4741/4742).
- Sumit: server LRU sliding window prototype for advisory Client-Replay-Hash (PR 4738) + metrics.
- docs-bot: draft docs explaining replay-hash vs Idempotency-Key and streaming retry semantics.
Renee: Thanks all, will monitor canary and post PR links when merged. Ping me if staging shows duplicates again. :thumbsup:
